Game 4 looms Monday at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse, with the top-seeded Pistons (60-22 regular season) leaning on their road wins in Games 1 and 2 despite Kevin Huerter remaining doubtful with a lingering left adductor strain; Cavaliers guard Sam Merrill is questionable with a hamstring issue but played limited minutes recently. Cleveland's home-court energy and stars' playoff form counter Detroit's depth and head-to-head edge, fueling trader consensus on a tightly contested matchup amid minimal injury disruptions to key rotations.

Lakers struggle offensively in the losses, now turning to home-court advantage for Game 3 on May 10 amid Jarred Vanderbilt's game-time decision (finger injury). OKC's No. 1 seed momentum, depth, and head-to-head playoff edge shape trader consensus, while Lakers' urgency to avoid a 3-0 hole, LeBron James' playoff experience, and crowd support introduce comeback volatility.

eventMetadata.context_description: Finland's Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen top Polymarket trader consensus at 45.1% implied probability to win Eurovision 2026 with their UMK-winning entry "Liekinheitin," fueled by the duo's Eurojury triumph on May 1, OGAE fan poll victory four days ago scoring 459 points, and buzz from initial Vienna rehearsals highlighting live violin and fierce staging. Denmark's Søren Torpegaard Lund follows at 12.8% after clinching Melodi Grand Prix in February with emotive ballad "Før vi går hjem," praised in recent rehearsals for vocal delivery. Greece's Akylas sits third at 12.0%, boosted by "Ferto"'s multilingual energy from Sing for Greece win, recently overtaking Denmark in odds. With semis on May 12 (Finland, Greece) and 14 (Denmark), and grand final May 16 at Wiener Stadthalle, rehearsal momentum and jury-televote splits will shape final standings.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: California Governor Gavin Newsom holds a clear lead in trader consensus at 24.8% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, driven by his consistent top performance in early national polls like Emerson College surveys showing 20-25% support, national fundraising prowess, and high-profile clashes with President Trump positioning him as a brawler in the party's anti-Republican fightback. Former Vice President Kamala Harris trails at 8.6% amid recent teases of another run at events like the National Action Network convention, while Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's 8.3% reflects progressive appeal among younger voters per youth polls. The wide-open field, fragmented below 10%, hinges on 2026 midterm results in battleground states, early primary polling in New Hampshire and Iowa, gubernatorial successes for swing-state executives like Josh Shapiro and Andy Beshear, and potential endorsements that could consolidate moderate or progressive blocs ahead of the 2027-2028 primary calendar.
